And it appears to me that for this reason he used a different language there: regarding leaving in salt he used "a third of an hour minus a thirtieth," so as not to be lenient regarding salting if one does not know how to be so exact and leave it a third of an hour by estimate to be stringent; and here he used "a quarter," so as to be stringent if one does not know how to be exact, that if he left without work a quarter of an hour it became chametz: all this is correct and clear according to Terumat HaDeshen and his company, and after him the later authorities followed. However, I saw that the Rambam and Bartenura wrote in the Mishnah of "These pass" that the measure of a mil is two-fifths of an hour of equal hours, end quote (meaning all hours are equal, each a twenty-fourth of day and night, not seasonal hours); and that is a third of an hour and a fifteenth of an hour, for when you divide the hour into fifteen parts, two-fifths of them are six parts, so it is a third of an hour and a fifteenth of an hour. And it appears that according to their view Maharil meant what he wrote, that it is a third of an hour and a bit more, for that is like the Rambam's view. But the matter is astonishing regarding such great ones, that they did not aim the reckoning according to the sugya of the Talmud that an average person walks ten parasangs in a day, as I wrote; at any rate the reckoning I wrote is a little less than a third of an hour. And the later authorities already noticed this astonishment: Maggid Mishneh, first chapter of Berachos, folio 7a; and Tiferes Yisrael, chapter 13 of Pesachim, Mishnah 2; and Chut HaShani at the end of the sefer in the accounting pamphlet. And Maggid Mishneh there answered that the Rambam is of the school who hold that the day is reckoned from sunrise to sunset, like the view of the Levush in siman 233 and siman 266; and when you deduct ten milin that Ulla said there in the Gemara an average person walks, namely five milin from dawn until sunrise and five milin from sunset until nightfall, thirty milin remain from sunrise until sunset, the twelve hours being reckoned thus according to his view; so the reckoning comes out to two-fifths, for there are six fifths in twelve hours, each hour into five parts, so each mil gets two-fifths. And one must say that the Rambam ruled like Ulla; for according to R' Yehuda, who holds that before sunrise and after sunset they walk only eight mil, thirty-two milin remain from sunrise until sunset, and then each mil does not get two-fifths, end quote of the content of his words there, though he wrote at length, see there. Now what he wrote, that the Rambam ruled like Ulla, his words are correct; and even though in the Talmud they left his words as a refutation, as he explained the matter there at length, and so it appears from Tosafos of the chapter "They would examine" (Sanhedrin folio 41) and Pesachim 11, and from Ra'am in Sefer Yere'im, and from Rashi at the beginning of Berachos. But what he wrote, that the Rambam's view is like the school who hold that the day is reckoned from sunrise to sunset: that is a great stretch, as Chut HaShani at the end of the responsa argued against this at length; and furthermore, on the contrary the Rambam's view is the opposite in several places in the commentary on the Mishnah and in his sefer Yad HaChazakah, as Menachat Kohen discussed at length in Chelek Mavo HaShemesh, maamar 1, chapter 2, see there. And in truth I have not fathomed the view of Maggid Mishneh and Responsa Chut HaShani and Magen Avraham in s.k. 3 who followed him and wrote that this depends on the dispute whether the day is reckoned from sunrise or from dawn. And anyone who examines and is precise in the sugya of the Talmud will see explicitly that the reckoning of the Rambam and Bartenura is a true reckoning according to the sugya, and the later authorities erred in this according to my humble opinion. And I will present the language of the Talmud and Rashi's explanation there on folio 93: we learn, Ulla said: from Modi'in to Jerusalem is fifteen milin (Rashi: since the Mishnah said regarding the Pesach offering, what is a distant journey: from Modi'in outward, that one cannot reach there from the time of slaughtering the Pesach, which is midday, until sunset). He holds like the statement of Rabbah bar bar Chanah who said in the name of R' Yochanan: how much does an average person walk in a day? Ten parasangs; from dawn until sunrise five milin; from sunset until nightfall five milin; thirty remain: fifteen from morning to midday and fifteen from midday to evening (Rashi: an average person walks on an average day of the tekufah of Nisan and Tishrei when day and night are equal). Thus it is clear explicitly that on the days of Nisan and Tishrei when days and nights are equal, an average person walks from sunrise until sunset thirty milin; and this is a peg that will not budge: for what we say that on the days of Nisan and Tishrei day and night are equal means specifically from sunrise until sunset, for from dawn until nightfall the day will be longer than the night by some hours, as the matter is visible to the eye by proof and by sense; and so it is in the Yerushalmi at the beginning of Berachos; and so Menachat Kohen discussed at length in Chelek Mavo HaShemesh, maamar 1, chapter 4, and that such is according to astronomy and nature, see there in maamar 1, chapter 11 at the end; and it is simple. And accordingly the Rambam's view aligns with the sugya of the Talmud and is precise according to the reckoning: for it is clear from this sugya that on the days of Nisan the day from sunrise until sunset, which is twelve equal hours, one can walk thirty mil, so each mil gets two-fifths of an hour. But if there is a difficulty upon the Rambam, it is this: since he ruled like Ulla, it turns out that from dawn until sunrise one can walk five milin, which is two hours according to the Rambam's reckoning; yet at the beginning of Berachos in the commentary on the Mishnah he wrote that it is only an hour and a fifth of an hour; and Responsa Chut HaShani similarly wonders at him there, see there. And one may say that the Rambam holds that the dispute of R' Yehuda and Ulla at first glance is difficult: how do they dispute with opposite reasonings against reality, that R' Yehuda holds that from sunrise until sunset they walk thirty-two milin, which proves he holds they walk faster than Ulla who holds they walk only thirty milin; and regarding before sunrise and after sunset R' Yehuda would hold they walk only four milin while Ulla holds five milin. Therefore the Rambam interprets that Ulla too holds one cannot walk five milin, and that he said five milin is according to those who rise early and stay late; and that he said "dawn" is only a fixed time, but in truth they rise early and stay late as R' Yehuda said there; and there are further ways to distinguish, see Menachat Kohen in Mavo HaShemesh. And he disagrees with R' Yehuda only regarding the walk from sunrise until sunset: according to R' Yehuda one can walk thirty-two milin and according to Ulla thirty milin. So the reckoning of the Rambam and Bartenura who ruled like Ulla is precise according to the sugya: two-fifths of an hour, namely a third of an hour and a fifteenth of an hour; and this is Maharil's view who wrote "a third of an hour and a bit more." And that he did not use exactly the Rambam's language "two-fifths of an hour" is perhaps because he is concerned for the view of poskim like R' Yehuda that an average person walks in twelve hours thirty-two milin; and see Menachat Kohen, who also wrote that many poskim hold like R' Yehuda. And if so, when you divide thirty-two milin among twelve hours of the day, for an hour and a half there are four milin; and in an hour and a half there are four thirds of an hour and half a third, so each mil gets a third of an hour; and afterward divide half a third, which is a sixth of an hour, into four parts, so it is a twenty-fourth of an hour; so each mil gets a third of an hour and a twenty-fourth of an hour. Therefore Maharil wrote simply that it is a bit more than a third of an hour and did not wish to write exactly in the Rambam's language. And however it may be, at any rate it is proven explicitly from what I wrote that the measure of a mil, both according to Ulla and according to R' Yehuda, is more than a third of an hour, both to be lenient as here regarding chametz and to be stringent regarding salting; and the view of the author of Terumat HaDeshen and Maharil, after whom the later authorities followed, cannot be settled at all according to the sugya (and it is even more astonishing regarding Menachat Kohen, that even though he saw and knew that on the days of Nisan and Tishrei when day and night are equal means from sunrise until sunset, as I wrote above in his name, even so he followed Terumat HaDeshen in this in maamar 8, chapter 1, see there; and this requires further study), unless we wish to say that Terumat HaDeshen stated his measure regarding seasonal hours that exist on the days of Nisan, namely from dawn until nightfall that time divided into twelve hours, and if so the reckoning also aligns with the Rambam's view in equal hours; but the plain language of Terumat HaDeshen here, and all the more so regarding salting, and all the other later authorities, does not so imply, and their words do not work at all according to the sugya. And regarding the Rambam we say that Moshe spoke well; and blessed is Hashem who guided me on the true path, and they left me room to elaborate on this, and I know a mere reckoning. And if one says, what need is there for all this length: let us see regarding an average person in what time he walks a mil: Tosafos already noticed such a difficulty in Shabbos folio 35a and answered that they were uncertain what is an average person; see there in Tosafos, and examine carefully. And a twentieth of an hour, etc. And this measure was stated only in a house that has no fire; but if there is fire in it, or any excess of warmth, it hastens to become chametz, and one must give heed according to the matter (Ateres Zekenim).
To hurry in the matter of making the matzos. And Shiltei Giborim wrote in siman 59: and one should not leave idle from the beginning of its kneading until he places it in the oven for the measure of four milin (and that is according to the reckoning I wrote in s.k. 10: an hour and a half according to R' Yehuda; and according to the Rambam it is an hour and a half and a tenth of an hour, for here there are eight fifths, thus an hour and two-fifths, and half is half an hour and half a fifth is a tenth of an hour); and so it is in the Yerushalmi, end quote. And so wrote the Bach in the name of Riaz, who further concluded: and it appears that even though the woman did not knead more than the measure and did not lift her hand from the dough at all, but rather was making very thin wafers and was lazy with them for the walking of four milin, this dough is forbidden even though no sign of chimutz is recognizable in them, end quote. And the Bach wrote, and this is his language: and this is not like the view of the Rambam, Rashba, our master, and other great ones, that so long as they are working with it, even all day, it does not become chametz; and at any rate he is dealing with kneading the measure of a dough and not more; and therefore it is not proper to rule prohibition for others b'dieved, but only to warn l'chatchilah to be concerned for the words of the greatest among the later authorities; and one who is stringent for himself even b'dieved, may blessing come upon him: it is proper to be concerned for his words, especially since Riaz is not alone in this law; and all the more so now that they are accustomed to knead doughs larger than the measure, as I wrote above at the end of siman 456. But b'dieved one should not rule prohibition against all those great ones, even if he kneaded more than the measure, for we do not find that they distinguished thus; and see above, siman 456.
That the idle periods combine. And Terumat HaDeshen wrote that working the hands and rolling with which they roll cancels the chimutz; but regarding piercing with which they pierce the matzos, even though it is work so that it not become chametz, nevertheless it does not cancel the idle periods like real work, end quote. And so is the consensus of the later authorities; and they further wrote in the name of Mahariv that one should not pass his hands over the matzos and rub them (and Kenesses HaGedolah wrote: and all the more so they do not do well when the multitude sticks a knife or a stick into the dough). And they further wrote in the name of Sefer Zichronos: and one should not begin to shape and roll the matzah until they sweep the oven, end quote. And it appears that this is not specifically all the oven's scrapings: for if he sweeps the whole oven and afterward begins to shape and roll the matzos and also pierce, through this the oven will sometimes cool greatly; rather one should not begin to shape until he begins to sweep, so that he can bake immediately; and so I have seen practiced in the house of the Gaon, my teacher's teacher. Also at first one should not begin to knead until some time after the oven was heated, so that immediately after kneading he can sweep the oven and begin to shape the matzos and bake immediately; and see what I wrote above, s.k. 5 and s.k. 6. And it is proper to warn the multitude about all such; and we do not say here "better that they be unintentional," since one can come to a prohibition according to the Torah, as the later authorities wrote. Nevertheless b'dieved there is no prohibition so long as it did not sit idle for the measure of chametz; and l'chatchilah one should be careful.
In a warm place that hastens to become chametz. For example in warm places, as clarified above in s.k. 9, see there; and see above, se'if 5, whether one should forbid even b'dieved if he kneaded near the mouth of the oven, and see there.
It is known that the second also became chametz. Even if it did not sit idle for the measure of a mil, even so we say that presumably there was some warmth there that caused it to become chametz quickly.
That there are cracks in it. And Responsa Maharam of Lublin, siman 105, wrote: if chimutz of cracking arose even in part of a dough, the entire dough is forbidden, end quote.
Its face whitened. Meaning of "whitened" is like "the upper whitened and not the lower" in the chapter "With what may one light"; and see Aruch, entry "kesef"; and it is a middle line between blackness and whiteness, which is the beginning of blackness, like green that they call in Ashkenaz "bleichlich"; and this is like a person whose hair stood from fear and trembling and whose appearance changed; and this is forbidden, but we are not expert in this measure (and see above in Hilchos Shabbos, siman 261); therefore one should not forbid afterward unless it sat idle for the measure of a mil without work. And so Kol Bo wrote explicitly on folio 48a, see there; and so is the implication of the Talmud in the chapter "These pass" regarding deaf dough.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ב) שם אין לשין וכו' ומי שאין לו מקום רחב בתוך הבית מותר לו ללוש המצות באמצעה של חצר מקום זריחת השמש ע"י פריסת אהלים וסדינים מלמעלה. תשו' בית יהודה סי' מ"ו. ברכ"י או' א' כס"א או' א'.
kaf_hachayyim.en: 2) There. One may not knead, etc. One who lacks a spacious place inside the house may knead matzos in the middle of a courtyard exposed to sunlight by spreading tents or sheets overhead. Responsa Beis Yehudah, siman 46; Birkei Yosef, subsection 1; Kisei Eliyahu, subsection 1.

mechaber.he: אם האשה שהיא לשה היא מקטפת במים לא תקטף באותן מים שמצננת בהם ידיה מפני שהם מתחממים ומחמיצים את העיסה אלא יהא לה כלי אחר מלא מים שתקטף בו: הגה ומיהו בעברה ולא צננה ידיה מותר: (רמב"ם פ"ה):
mechaber.en: If a woman is kneading the dough, she should shape it with water [but] not the water which she cooled her hands with because this water has been heated [from this action] and will leaven the dough. Rather she should have another vessel filled with water for shaping it. REMA: however, [where] she transgressed and did not cool her hands, it is permitted. {Rama: (RAMBAM perek 5)}

baer_heitev.he:
מקטפת. פירוש שטחה פני החררה במים. ואין נוהגין במדינות אלו בקיטוף המצות במים:
שמצננת. הב"ח מסכים דצריכה לצנן ידיה בשעת התעסקות בעיסה אפילו אינה עסוקה בתנור וכ"כ הש"ל. אכן דעת הר"ן והמ"מ אינו כן דכל שאינה מתחממת מחום התנור ואח"כ נוגעת בעיסה א"צ לצנן כלל (ובדיעבד אין לאסור. אחרונים) וכן המנהג שלא לצנן הידים כשעוסקים בלישת העיסה וכן נ"ל. ח"י ע"ש:
baer_heitev.en:
One who is shaping [kituf]. Meaning she smoothes the face of the cake with water. And in these lands they are not accustomed to trim the matzos with water.
That cools. The Bach agrees that she must cool her hands while working with the dough even if she is not busy with the oven; and so wrote Shiltei Giborim. However, the view of the Ran and Maggid Mishneh is not so: so long as she is not warming from the heat of the oven and afterward touching the dough, she need not cool at all (and b'dieved one should not forbid; later authorities). And likewise the custom is not to cool the hands when working at kneading the dough; and so it appears to me; Chok Yaakov, see there.

beer_hagolah.he: מימרא דרבא שם מ"ג וכפי הר"ן
beer_hagolah.en: A statement of Rava there, 43, and according to the Ran.

beur_hagra.he: ס"ג ומיהו. דהרמב"ם סובר דפלוגתא דעברה ולשה לא קאי אלא בחמי חמה ובמים הגרופין מדהביא ראיה מאין לותתין דדמיא להו:
beur_hagra.en: Se'if 3: However. For the Rambam holds that the dispute of "if she passed and kneaded" applies only to water heated by the sun and to drawn water, since he brought proof from "one may not moisten," which is similar to them.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ג] כנגד החלון וכו'. אבל מן הצד מותר (חק יעקב), ולפי מה שכתבתי ריש סימן זה יש ליזהר:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [3] Opposite the window, etc. But from the side it is permitted (Chok Yaakov); and according to what I wrote at the beginning of this siman, one should be careful.

magen_avraham.he:
מקטפת. במדינות אלו נוהגין שלא לקטף המצות במים (ד"מ):
ומיהו בעברה כו'. משמע דלכתחלה צריכה לצנן ידיה והיינו כשהיא עוסקת עם התנור ועוסקת ג"כ אח"כ בבצק:
magen_avraham.en:
One who is shaping [kituf]. In these lands they are accustomed not to trim the matzos with water (Darkei Moshe).
However, if she transgressed, etc. It is implied that l'chatchilah she must cool her hands; and that is when she is working with the oven and also afterward works with the dough.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(כד) מקטפת - ר"ל שטחה פני החררה במים:
(כה) שמצננת - דצריך לצנן הידים בשעת לישה לכתחלה משום דהידים מתחממים מרוב העסק ומתחמם העיסה מהידים:
(כו) אלא יהא לה וכו' - ובמדינות אלו נוהגין שלא לקטוף המצות במים [ד"מ]:
(כז) ולא ציננה - וה"ה אם עברה וקטפה את המצות במים שציננה ידיה ג"כ נראה לכאורה שמותר בדיעבד. ודע דיש פוסקים דס"ל דלא מצרכינן כלל לצנן הידים בשעת לישה אפילו לכתחלה ולא הצריכו לצנן ידים לכתחלה אלא אם אותה שלשה אופה ג"כ ומשום דמתקרבת לתנור ידיה חמימות וכשלשה אח"כ חששו חכמים שלא תחמם העיסה בידיה וכתבו שכן המנהג שלא להחמיר ומיהו כ"ז בסתם אבל במרגשת שנתחממו ידיה לכו"ע צריך לצנן. ואפילו בסתם טוב לכתחלה להחמיר שכן הוא דעת כמה ראשונים:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(24) One who is shaping [kituf] - That is to say, she smoothes the face of the cake with water.
(25) That cools - For one must cool the hands at the time of kneading l'chatchilah, because the hands warm from much work and the dough warms from the hands.
(26) Rather she should have, etc. - And in these lands they are accustomed not to trim the matzos with water [Darkei Moshe].
(27) And she did not cool - And the same applies if she transgressed and trimmed the matzos with water with which she cooled her hands: it also appears at first glance that it is permitted b'dieved. And know that there are poskim who hold that we do not require at all cooling the hands at the time of kneading even l'chatchilah, and they required cooling the hands l'chatchilah only if the one who kneads also bakes, because as she draws near the oven her hands are warm, and when she kneads afterward the Sages feared that she warm the dough with her hands; and they wrote that such is the custom not to be stringent. However, all this is in an ordinary case; but if she feels that her hands warmed, according to all opinions she must cool. And even in an ordinary case it is good l'chatchilah to be stringent, for such is the view of several early authorities.

peri_megadim.he: ואם עט״ז ואפילו עסק בה כל שעה כל שרואה אחת החמיצה בעסק כזה א״כ הוא ג״כ חמץ כ״כ ז״ל. וי״א ד׳ מילין אוסרין אף בעסק ויבואר אי״ה במ״א. ועשו״ת מהר״מ מלובלין ז״ל סימן ק״ה והח״י אות ט״ו הביאו כל שיש סי׳ חימוץ במקצת עיסה כולה אסורה:
peri_megadim.en: And if. See Taz: and even if he worked on it the whole time, so long as one sees that part of it became chametz with such work, then it too is chametz; so he wrote, of blessed memory. And some say that four milin forbid even with work, and this will be explained, if Hashem wills, in Magen Avraham. And see Responsa Maharam of Lublin, of blessed memory, siman 105; and Chok Yaakov letter 15 brought [the ruling that] wherever there is a sign of chimutz in part of a dough, the entire [dough] is forbidden.

turei_zahav.he: מקטפת. פי' שטחה במים פני החררה לא תקטף באותן המים שמצננת בהם הידים מפני שהם מתחממים אבל כל שאינה מקטפת במים לא הצריכוהו לדקדק אם ידיה חמין באין חשש חימוץ בכל ולכך פי' הרמב"ם דלא אמרי' שצריכה לצנן ידיה אלא כשהיא אופה לפי שידיה מתחממים מחמת חום התנור כ"כ הר"ן וה"ה:
turei_zahav.en: Shaping. Meaning: she flattens it with water on the face of the flat cake; she should not shape with that water with which she cools her hands because they become heated; but whenever she does not shape with water, they did not require her to be precise whether her hands are hot, for there is no concern of chametzing in every case; and therefore Rambam explained that we do not say she must cool her hands.

chok_yaakov.he:
מקטפת. פירוש שטחה פני החררה במים ואין נוהגין במדינות אלו בקיטוף המצות במים:
שמצטננת בהם ידים הב"ח מסכים דצריכה לצנן ידיה בשעת התעסקות בעיסה אפילו אינה עסוקה בתנור לפי שמתחממין ידי' מהתעסקות בעיסה ושכן דעת רוב הפוסקים וכ"כ הש"ל ע"ש אכן דעת הר"ן והמ"מ אינו כן דכל שאינה מתחממות מחום התנור ואח"כ נוגעת בעיסה אינה צריכה לצנן כלל וכן המנהג שלא לצנן הידים כשעוסקין בלישת העיסה וכן נ"ל לדקדק קצת ממשמעות לשון הש"ס דקאמר האשה צריכה שני כלים האחת שמקטפת בו ואחת שמצטננת בו ואם איתא דצונן קאי משום התעסקות בעיסה הוי ליה למימר להיפך דזה הוא קודם הקיטוף וק"ל:
chok_yaakov.en:
One who is shaping [kituf]. Meaning she smoothes the face of the cake with water; and in these lands they are not accustomed to trim the matzos with water.
In which the hands are cooled The Bach agrees that she must cool her hands while working with the dough even if she is not busy with the oven, because the hands warm from working with the dough; and such is the view of most poskim; and so wrote Shiltei Giborim, see there. However, the view of the Ran and Maggid Mishneh is not so: so long as she is not warming from the heat of the oven and afterward touching the dough, she need not cool at all. And likewise the custom is not to cool the hands when working at kneading the dough; and so it appears to me to be somewhat precise from the implication of the Talmud's language, which says a woman needs two vessels, one with which she trims and one with which she cools; and if it were that cooling is because of working with the dough, it should have said the reverse, for that comes before the trimming; and this is sufficient.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ג) שם. אין לשין במקום השמש. ואם עברה ולשה תחת השמש הפת מותר. הרמב"ם פ"ה. וכ"פ הש"ע לקמן סעי' ה' וכתב הפר"ח לקמן בסעי' ה' וכ"ש כשלש ביום המעונן תחת הרקיע ומסתמא נמי דה"ה אם לש סמוך לפי התנור וכיוצא דבדיעבד מותר לדעת הרמב"ם. וכ"כ המש"ז או' א' לדעת הש"ע ה"ה ביום המעונן שרי בדיעבד יעו"ש וכ"כ החמ"מ או' א' אבל דעת הרא"ש בס"פ כל שעה לאסור בעברה ולשה תחת השמש, והביאו ב"י. וכ"פ הב"ח וכתב דאסור אף דיעבד ושוגג וה"ה ביום המעונן דדינו כלש בחמה וכ"ש דאסור אף בדיעבד בלש קרוב לפי תנורים שלנו שפיהן מן הצד והעיסה מתחממת מיד אצל פי התנור יעו"ש והביאו מ"א ס"ק ט"ו וכתב ונ"ל דוקא כשהוחמה העיסה עכ"ל והביאו ח"י או' כ"ו. וכ"כ א"ר או' ו' חמ"מ שם. ר"ז או' ח' ח"א כלל קכ"ח או' י"ז. מ"ב או' כ"א. ועיין במגן האלף או' ו' שכתב דבמזיד יש להחמיר אפי' לא הוחמה העיסה כיון דכל הלישה היתה בחמה מיהו בהתחילה בחמה וגמרה אח"כ במקום אחר אפשר דאין להחמיר עכ"ל אמנם מדברי הפו' הנז' משמע דאין חילוק אלא כל שלא הוחמה בדיעבד שרי וכ"כ הר"ז שם דאם לא הוחמה מותרת אפי' לש במזיד ומשמע שם בר"ז דאף אם הוחמה אינו אסור רק באכילה אבל בהנאה שרי יעו"ש ונראה בזה דהכל לפי העניין דאם אנחנו רואים שהוחם הרבה אז יש לאסור אף בהנאה אם הוא בתוך הפסח או בע"פ אחר זמן איסורו. ועיין לעיל סי' תנ"ה או' ע"א.
kaf_hachayyim.en: 3) There. One may not knead in sunlight. If a woman transgressed and kneaded in sunlight, the bread is permitted. Rambam, chapter 5. The Shulchan Aruch likewise rules below in se'if 5. Peri Chadash writes there in se'if 5 that this is certainly so if one kneaded beneath the open sky on a cloudy day. It may also be assumed that according to Rambam, if one kneaded near the mouth of an oven or in a similar place, the dough is permitted after the fact. Mishbetzos Zahav, subsection 1, likewise writes that according to the Shulchan Aruch, dough kneaded on a cloudy day is permitted after the fact. See there. Chemed Moshe, subsection 1, writes likewise. Rosh at the end of the chapter Kol Sha'ah, however, prohibits dough that was kneaded in sunlight, as cited by Beis Yosef. Bach rules likewise and writes that it is prohibited even after the fact and even when done inadvertently. The same applies on a cloudy day, whose law is like kneading in sunlight. It is certainly prohibited after the fact if kneaded near the mouth of our ovens, whose openings are on the side, because the dough warms immediately near the oven opening. See there. Magen Avraham, subsection 15, cites this and writes, 'It appears to me that this applies specifically when the dough became warm.' Chok Yaakov, subsection 26, cites his words. Eliyah Rabbah, subsection 6; Chemed Moshe, there; Shulchan Aruch HaRav, subsection 8; Chayei Adam, rule 128, subsection 17; Mishnah Berurah, subsection 21, write likewise. Magen HaElef, subsection 6, writes that when one acted deliberately, one should be stringent even if the dough did not become warm, since the entire kneading was performed in sunlight. If one began in sunlight but finished elsewhere, however, it is possible that one need not be stringent. These are his words. The authorities cited above, however, imply that there is no distinction: whenever the dough did not become warm, it is permitted after the fact. Shulchan Aruch HaRav there explicitly writes that if it did not become warm, it is permitted even if one kneaded deliberately. He also implies that even when it did become warm, it is prohibited only for consumption but permitted for benefit. See there. It appears that everything depends upon the circumstances. If we see that it became very warm, it should be prohibited even for benefit if this occurred during Pesach or on the eve of Pesach after chametz became prohibited. See above, siman 455, subsection 71.

mechaber.he: אם לש אחר זמן איסור חמץ אלו המים עם שאר המים שרוחצים בהם העריבה לא ישפכם אלא במקום מדרון כדי שלא יתקבצו במקום א' ויחמיץ: הגה והכלים שמתקנים בהם המצות והסכין שחותכין בו העיסה יגרדם תמיד בשעת עשייה שלא ידבק בהן הבצק ולאחר עשייה ידיחם וינגבם היטב לחזור ולתקן בהם פעם שנית (מהרי"ל) וזהו עדיף טפי ממה שנוהגי' לגרדן כי אי אפשר לנקותן היטב ע"י גרידה והמחמיר יגרדן ואח"כ ידיחן (ד"ע) ובי"ט מותר לעשותו על ידי עכו"ם ואם אין עכו"ם יטילם לצונן או יתנם לתנור שיאפה הבצק שעליהם והערבות שאפשר לתת דבר בתוכו מותר להדיח וכן כל כיוצא בזה ויש ליזהר בעריבה שלשין בה שלא יהיה בו שום גומא או סדק שלא יוכל לנקרו אחר הלישה ותחמיץ ואח"כ כשחוזר ולש בו מתערב בבצק (מהרי"ל) ולא יתן העריבה על כר או כסת צמר בשעת הלישה שמחמם העריבה אבל על של עור שרי: (מהרי"ו):
mechaber.en: If [the dough] was kneaded after the beginning of when leaven becomes forbidden, the [hand cooling] waters along with other water used for washing the trough, one shouldn't spill them except in a sloped area so that they shouldn't accumulate in one place and leaven. REMA: and the vessels which one fixes for Matzo use, and the knife which one cuts the dough in portions should constantly be scraped at the time of production so that dough does not adhere to it. After, he should scrub them and dry them well, so that he may return and fix them for use a second time . This is ideal compared to the practice of scraping it, for it's impossible to clean it well by scraping it. A strict person will scrape it and afterward will scrub it. . On Yom Tov, it's permitted for him to [clean them] via a gentile and if there is not a gentile, one should dispatch them to the cold or place them in the oven so the dough [on them] will bake. Troughs, where it's possible to put something inside them it's implied that it's permissible [to wash it] and other similar things. One should be cautious with a trough which one kneads in, that there shouldn't be any cracks or crevice which one will be unable to pick [all the dough out of] after kneading, and it will leaven and afterward when he returns to knead in the trough, it will mix with the dough . one shouldn't place the trough on a pillow or wool cover when kneading, for it will heat the trough but on leather is permissible. {Rama: (MAHA"RIL) (his own words) (MAHA"RIL)}

baer_heitev.he:
עשייה. וכתב המ"א דלא כמו שנוהגין העולם שלא לגררם עד אחר עשיי' כי אע"פ שאין שוהין שיעור מיל מ"מ לכתחלה אסור לכן יעמוד אחד על גביהן שיגרד תמיד כל כלי בשעת הנחתו ע"כ ועח"י:
ידיחן. והמרדה א"צ להדיחו. דרשות מהרי"ל:
לצונן. ויכבד אותם שיהיו למטה מן המים ואל יצופו למעלה. מהרי"ו ועיין ח"י:
שיאפה. דהיינו באותה תנור שהוסק לאפיה ולא להסיק מחדש בשביל כלים אלו ח"י. ומ"מ אסור לאכול הבצק ההוא דבצד השני ובסדקים לא נאפה יפה מהרי"ל. וכתב המ"א ונ"ל שיבטל החמץ קודם שיחמיץ או יתן הכלים עם הבצק במתנה לעכו"ם ואם צריך לאפות שנית בי"ט פשיטא דשרי להדיחן אבל אסור לגורדן כמ"ש סוף סימן שכ"ג:
סדק. יש מצפין השלחן והעמילה בטס של מתכות ויש שעושין מאבן חלקה כדי שתקרר. ספר זכרונות. ואחר כל עיסה ועיסה ידיח ידיו והספל יפה וינגבו במפה אא"כ לש מיד בלי הפסק ובשל"ה כתב דנכון שיכין ב' כלים ומיד אחר לישה הראשונה יהא מוכן אחד לרחוץ הכלי היטב ועיסה השניה ימדוד בכלי שני וכן חוזר חלילה ע"כ. (וח"י כתב דלא ראיתי נוהגין כן דא"כ בין מצה למצה ודקירה לדקירה נמי יש לחוש ע"ש עד לא נתנה תורה למה"ש). ונ"ל דוקא בכלי נחושת שייך זה דיכול לקנחו אבל של עץ דא"א לקנח שלא יהא בו עדיין מים מהדחה לא שייך זה. כתב מהרי"ל שלא להתחיל ללוש שניה עד אשר הוסק התנור שנית וביני ביני ירחוץ הספל וכל הכלים. וכתב מהרי"ו אותו שנותן הקמח ידיח ידיו וכן אותו שתיקן המצות. הסדין צריך להחליף בין לישה ללישה ואם עושה על דף בלא סדין ויש נקבים בדף צריך לסותמם שלא יכניס בה הבצק. וגם במרדה לא יהיה סדק או חריץ וע"ל סימן תנ"א סעיף י"ח וא"ז כתב דטוב יותר לעשות המצות על דף מלעשות על סדין וכ"כ הט"ז בסי' תנ"ג ס"ק ה' עיין שם. והעולם נוהגין לעשות על סדין לפי שרוב שלחנות אינם חלקים:
צמר. אבל בגד צמר שרי מ"א. ובדיעבד בכל ענין ליכא איסור. ח"י:
baer_heitev.en:
Production. And Magen Avraham wrote: not like the practice of the world, who do not scrape them until after production; for even though they do not sit idle for the measure of a mil, nevertheless l'chatchilah it is forbidden; therefore one should stand over them who will scrape every utensil continually at the time it is set down, end quote. And see Chok Yaakov.
He should rinse them. And the baker's peel need not be rinsed; Derashos Maharil.
Into cold water. And he should weigh them down so that they be below the water and not float on top; Mahariv. And see Chok Yaakov.
That it bake. That is, in that same oven that was heated for baking, and one should not heat anew for these utensils; Chok Yaakov. And nevertheless it is forbidden to eat that dough, for on the other side and in the cracks it was not baked well; Maharil. And Magen Avraham wrote: and it appears to me that one should bitul the chametz before it becomes chametz, or give the utensils with the dough as a gift to a non-Jew. And if he needs to bake a second time on Yom Tov, obviously it is permitted to rinse them, but it is forbidden to scrape them, as is written at the end of siman 323.
A crack. Some plate the table and the kneading-board with a metal sheet, and some make [it] of smooth stone so that it cool; Sefer Zichronos. And after every dough one should wash his hands and the basin well and dry them with a cloth, unless he kneads immediately without interruption. And in the Shelah he wrote that it is proper to prepare two vessels, and immediately after the first kneading one should be ready to wash the vessel thoroughly, and the second dough should be measured in the second vessel, and so he alternates, end quote. (And Chok Yaakov wrote that I have not seen people practicing thus, for if so, between matzah and matzah and piercing and piercing one should also be concerned, see there, until [he says] the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.) And it appears to me that this applies specifically with a copper vessel, which one can wipe dry; but with wood, where one cannot wipe so that there not still be rinse-water in it, this does not apply. Maharil wrote not to begin kneading a second [dough] until the oven has been heated a second time, and in the meantime wash the basin and all the utensils. And Mahariv wrote: the one who puts the flour should wash his hands, and likewise the one who shaped the matzos. The sheet must be changed between one kneading and the next; and if one works on a board without a sheet and there are holes in the board, one must seal them so that dough not enter them. And also in the peel there should not be a crack or groove; and see above, siman 451, se'if 18. And Or Zarua wrote that it is better to make the matzos on a board than on a sheet; and so wrote the Taz in siman 453, s.k. 5, see there. And the world is accustomed to make them on a sheet, because most tables are not smooth.
Wool. But a woolen garment is permitted; Magen Avraham. And b'dieved in every case there is no prohibition; Chok Yaakov.
